newsitem.title: USA: Pamela Harriman's estate to be auctioned off.
newsitem.headline: Pamela Harriman's estate to be auctioned off.

text.p: Didn't get a chance to buy one of Jaqueline Kennedy Onassis's baubles at auction and don't think you will fit into one of Princess Diana's dresses?

Don't fret. There is an alternative. The possessions of the late ambassador to France, Pamela Harriman, a leading society and Democratic Party figure, will be auctioned off in New York in a two-day sale starting on May 19, Sotheby's announced on Tuesday.

The sale will include her paintings, French, English and Italian furniture, porcelain, silver, crystal, candelabras, medallions, books, photographs, wine and signed photographs and paintings by her former father-in-law, Winston Churchill, Sotheby's said.

It was the third major sale announced for the upcoming spring auction season in the last three weeks, with Christie's previously announcing that it would sell Princess Diana's dresses to benefit charities on June 25. It will also sell one of the great private collections of impressionist art, the John and Francine Loeb collection on May 12.

Sotheby's president, Diana Brooks, said the auction house will be notifying participants at their widely successful sale last year of Mrs. Onassis possessions of the Harriman sale. "This sale will generate a good deal of enthusiasm, but it is hard to guess the extent. At this stage we are still sorting things," Brooks said.
She said it was too early to give a sale estimate. Sotheby's real estate division will privately sell Harriman's homes in the Georgetown section of Washington and an estate in Middleburg, Virginia.

Harriman died on Feb. 5 at age 76 in Paris. A member of a British aristocratic family, she was married to Churchill's son, Randolph, Broadway producer Leland Haywood and American millionaire diplomat and former New York Gov. W. Averell Harriman.
She was also reported to have had liaisons with several millionaires and prominent industralists.
After her marriage to Harriman, she become prominent in the Democratic Party and her Georgetown home become a salon for many prominent political figures, including President Bill Clinton.
Among the paintings to be sold are works by John Singer Sargent, George Seurat, Andre Derain, Walt Kuhn and Winston Churchill.
Sotheby's said her property was being put up for sale by her estate and it did not know how the proceeds would be disposed of.
The Harriman sale will come a week after the sale of the Loeb collection of impressionist art, which experts say might break the $110 million record for a single-owner collection.
Christie's current estimate is that the 30-piece collection will take in about $80 million.

It includes a rare Cezanne portrait of his wife which is estimated to sell for $25 million, and a self-portrait of Manet which could go for $15 million. Reuters recently incorrectly reported the estimate of the Manet at $25 million.

The auction house declined to give an estimate for the sale of 80 gowns and evening dresses owned by Princess Diana which she has given Christie's to sell on June 25. The British press has reported that the dresses could sell for up to $50,000 each.
